title: Two-paddle tennis
hints: The closest point of a rectangle to a circle's centre is the centre clamped to the rectangle on each axis; the circle overlaps when that point is within the radius.
"Moving towards the paddle" is just the sign of `vel.x`: negative for the left paddle, positive for the right.
`std::cos` and `std::sin` take radians, not degrees: convert with `angle * 3.14159265f / 180.0f`. The speed is the length of `vel`, `std::sqrt(vel.x * vel.x + vel.y * vel.y)`, as in lesson 1.04.
requirements: Paddles are clamped to the field, and the ball bounces off the top and bottom.
A paddle hit speeds the ball up (to at most 900) and aims it by where it hit the paddle.
A ball moving away from a paddle does not bounce off it again.
Points, serves and the winner follow the rules above.
stretch: Add a serve delay of one second after each point, a "spin" that adds some of the paddle's own vertical speed to the ball, and a sound and screen shake on every hit.
